sections.h2: Where is Greenwich, Connecticut, and how large is it?
sections.html:
Greenwich is the southwesternmost town in Connecticut and in New England, a town of 63,518 people in the 2020 census. It borders Port Chester and Rye Brook and North Castle in New York, Stamford to the east, and Long Island Sound to the south.

The total area is 67.2 square miles, 47.8 of land and 19.4 of water, so water makes up nearly 29 percent of the town. Wikipedia notes that this is twice the size of Manhattan. ZIP codes are 06830, 06831, 06870 and 06878.

Greenwich is one town and one taxing body, but it is made of distinct sections, and that matters when a buyer asks where a house sits.

  • The Census Bureau recognizes nine places inside the town: Byram, Cos Cob, Glenville, Indian Field, Old Greenwich, Pemberwick, Riverside, Rock Ridge and the central Greenwich area.
  • Cos Cob, Old Greenwich and Riverside have their own postal names and ZIP codes.
  • Informal areas include the Back Country, Mid-Country, Belle Haven, Chickahominy, Mianus, Banksville and the Fourth Ward.

sections.h2: What is the history of Greenwich?
sections.html:
Agents Robert Feake and Daniel Patrick bought the land from the Siwanoy in 1640 for 25 English coats, on behalf of the New Haven Colony. The Connecticut General Assembly declared Greenwich a township on May 11, 1665.

General Israel Putnam made his well-known escape from British forces in Greenwich on February 26, 1779. The town also has a 2001 landmark in beach law: after Leydon v. Greenwich, the town had to open all four of its beaches, including Greenwich Point, to non-residents.

Those four beaches on the Sound are Greenwich Point, Byram Beach, Island Beach and Great Captain Island, which includes the southernmost point in Connecticut.

Finance dominates. Greenwich is home to many hedge funds and financial services firms, drawn by a residential setting close to Manhattan, according to Wikipedia.

TypeExamples listed by Wikipedia
Investment firmsAQR Capital, Silver Point Capital, Viking Global Investors, Tudor Investment Corporation
Insurance and brokerageW. R. Berkley, Interactive Brokers
Other major institutionsGreenwich Hospital, Hyatt Regency, Eversource Energy, Brunswick School

The list above names examples and is not a ranking by headcount.

sections.h2: How does Greenwich weather affect a house?
sections.html:
Greenwich has a humid continental climate that sits close to humid subtropical. Average annual precipitation is 50.45 inches, and average snowfall is 28 inches a year.

Snow is not even across town. Wikipedia reports that the area north of the Merritt Parkway usually gets heavier snowfall than the coast, where Long Island Sound moderates winter weather. January highs average 35 degrees and July highs 82.

  • Areas north of the Merritt Parkway, such as the Back Country, can see more snow than the shoreline.
  • Coastal sections such as Old Greenwich, Riverside and Byram sit near the water, so flood zone status is a standard question for buyers.

We did not open an official Greenwich page on flood or zoning rules. The town's Planning and Zoning and Wetlands offices can answer for a specific address.

sections.h2: How do trains, highways and schools serve Greenwich?
sections.html:
Metro-North's New Haven Line has four Greenwich stations: Greenwich, Cos Cob, Riverside and Old Greenwich. An express train to Grand Central takes about 50 minutes and a local about 60.

Interstate 95 crosses the south end of town with exits 2 through 5. The Boston Post Road (Route 1) and the Merritt Parkway also run through, and Westchester County Airport is about 15 minutes by car from the town center.

Greenwich Public Schools has one high school, Greenwich High School, three middle schools (Central, Eastern and Western) and eleven elementary schools, including Cos Cob, Glenville, Old Greenwich, Riverside and North Street. Wikipedia reports that about 25 to 30 percent of K-12 residents attend private schools, a high share for the region.

sections.h2: When are Greenwich property taxes due?
sections.html:
Greenwich bills real estate, personal property and motor vehicle tax together. The Tax Collector's page says bills were mailed June 17, payment is due July 1, and the bill is delinquent after August 3.

The office is in Town Hall, 101 Field Point Road, Room 145, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 am to 3:30 pm, and the phone is 203-622-7891.

Payment methodFee noted on the page
In person or by mail (check, money order, cash in person)None listed
Online, electronic funds transfer$2.00 per transaction, paid to the vendor
Online, card, Apple Pay or Google Pay2.50 percent of the payment, paid to the vendor
Returned payment$20.00 plus possible interest

Delinquent real estate bills carry interest through a stated date, and the page says any property with a balance due is liened in May. An owner who is behind can ask the office for a payoff figure before choosing a closing date.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Greenwich assessment?
sections.html:
You file with the elected Board of Assessment Appeals, not the Assessor. The Board's page says the Assessor's Office will not accept appeal forms.

For the 2025 Grand List the real estate and personal property deadline was February 20, 2026 at 5:00 pm, citing Connecticut General Statutes section 12-111. Hearings began in March 2026 in person at Town Hall. The next deadline will be posted for the 2026 Grand List, so check before assuming a date.

  • The appeal covers the assessment only. The tax amount comes from the mill rate, which the Board of Estimate and Taxation sets in May.
  • The Board can raise, lower or leave an assessment alone, and mails decisions about two weeks after hearings end.
  • An owner who disagrees can go to Connecticut Superior Court within 60 days of the notice.
  • The Board may skip hearings for commercial, industrial, utility or apartment property assessed above $1,000,000.

The Board has five elected members, chosen every two years in odd years.

sections.h2: What is the conveyance tax filing when a Greenwich house sells?
sections.html:
The seller or the seller's attorney files the state's Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded, and Greenwich's town code on that form is 057. The Department of Revenue Services says tax is due when consideration reaches $2,000 unless the transfer is exempt.

Exempt transfers on the state list include a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence, a principal residence sold for too little to cover its mortgages and tax liens, and transfers between spouses.

We left out the rates because we did not open a page that states them for Greenwich. Ask your closing agent or the Town Clerk's office.

sections.h2: What do Greenwich sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Greenwich is a mix of coastal sections, village centers and the Back Country, so a seller's situation depends heavily on the street.

  • Houses with deferred repairs can be hard to sell on the open market.
  • Estates may need time to settle ownership before listing.
  • Owners behind on tax may face a May lien and need a closing date that clears it.

A cash sale is one option for owners who want a fixed closing date. The buyer takes the house as-is, and any open tax is paid from the proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Greenwich property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due July 1 and bills are delinquent after August 3, according to the Tax Collector's page. Check the page each year, since mailing and due dates can change.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Greenwich assessment appeal?
faqs.a: With the Board of Assessment Appeals, not the Assessor. The Board's email is boardofassessmentappeals@greenwichct.org, and its page says the Assessor's Office will not accept appeal forms.

faqs.q: What was the last Greenwich appeal deadline?
faqs.a: For the 2025 Grand List it was February 20, 2026 at 5:00 pm. Ask the Board for the date that applies to the 2026 Grand List.

faqs.q: Who sets the Greenwich mill rate?
faqs.a: The Board of Estimate and Taxation sets it in May, per the Board of Assessment Appeals page. We did not confirm the current rate.

faqs.q: What happens to Greenwich real estate that stays delinquent?
faqs.a: The Tax Collector's page says delinquent real estate bills include interest through a set date and any property with a balance due is liened in May. Contact the office for your payoff.

faqs.q: What is the Greenwich town code on the state conveyance form?
faqs.a: The code is 057 on Form OP-236, per the Department of Revenue Services.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenwich house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax is paid from the proceeds at closing, and a cash sale can close on a date you choose.
